title: One-week study plan
intro: Seven days, about two hours a day. The free videos give you coverage, the browser labs give you hands-on, and the app gives you recall and timing. Nothing here needs a cluster of your own.
note: Every link was checked for status, title and duration on the date above. Where something looks free but is not, that is stated.

days.title: Architecture and Installation
days.summary: Everything else assumes the component model. Learn which binary runs where before touching policy.

items.title: Cilium Week, Session 1: Architecture and Installation
items.why: Walks the whole architecture and installation domain in one sitting.

items.title: Getting Started with Cilium
items.why: Installs Cilium and runs the connectivity test. The exam asks what cilium status and cilium connectivity test actually do.

items.title: Cilium IPAM
items.why: IPAM is a named architecture competency. Tunnelling versus direct routing, and where pod addresses actually come from.

items.title: Practice: Architecture
items.meta: In this app · filter by domain
items.why: Architecture is the largest domain at 20%.

days.title: Measure yourself, then Network Policy
days.summary: Take the baseline first. It is the only score that measures you rather than the generator, and doing it now means the final delta is honest.

items.title: Blind evaluation: baseline
items.meta: In this app · 102 questions, no feedback
items.why: Questions the app never teaches from. Do not retake this until day 7.

items.title: Cilium Week, Session 2: Network policy and observability
items.why: Covers the identity model, enforcement modes and L7 policy.

items.title: Practice: Network Policy
items.meta: In this app · filter by domain
items.why: 18% of the exam and the domain people most often fail.

days.title: Write policy, then observe it
days.summary: Reading policy syntax is not the same as writing it. Then use Hubble to see the drops you created.

items.title: Isovalent Enterprise: Network Policies
items.why: Namespaced and cluster-wide rules, explicit-deny precedence and HTTP L7 behaviour, checked with Hubble. The lab has been refreshed with Enterprise tooling (Timescape, Isopolicy); the policy composition and L7 verdicts are the CCA-relevant parts.

items.title: Cilium IPv6 Networking and Observability
items.why: Hubble flows, filters and verdicts, including the drop reasons.

items.title: Golden Signals with Hubble and Grafana
items.why: L7 protocol visibility is a named observability competency, and this lab shows it becoming metrics without touching the app.

items.title: Policy Enforcement Modes
items.why: Default, always and never, and the per-direction rule. Questions on this appear constantly.

items.title: Practice: Network Observability
items.meta: In this app · filter by domain
items.why: 10% and mostly recall of Hubble flags.

days.title: Service Mesh and Gateway API
days.summary: The largest domain you are least likely to have touched. Sidecarless is the point, not a detail.

items.title: Isovalent CCA playlist: the Gateway API demos
items.meta: Traffic splitting, header modifier, cross-namespace routing, TLS passthrough
items.why: Short demos, each one a question type. Pick the Gateway API entries.

items.title: Cilium Gateway API
items.why: GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute by doing rather than reading.

items.title: Cilium Transparent Encryption with IPSec and WireGuard
items.why: Encryption in transit is a named competency, and IPsec versus WireGuard is a favourite distinction.

items.title: Practice: Service Mesh
items.meta: In this app · filter by domain
items.why: 16% of the exam.

days.title: Cluster Mesh and BGP
days.summary: Two small domains that are easy to neglect and easy to score on, because the facts are discrete.

items.title: Cilium Week, Session 3: BGP, Service mesh and Cluster mesh
items.why: The only free video that covers BGP and Cluster Mesh together.

items.title: Cilium Cluster Mesh
items.why: Global services, affinity and cross-cluster failover.

items.title: BGP on Cilium
items.why: Peering, advertisement and the current four CRDs.

items.title: Practice: Cluster Mesh and BGP
items.meta: In this app · filter by domain
items.why: 16% between them, and the cheapest marks on the paper.

days.title: eBPF and everything you got wrong
days.summary: eBPF is only 10% but it underpins half the other answers. Then clear your wrong-answer backlog.

items.title: Getting started with eBPF
items.why: Programs, maps and hook points, which is what the exam asks about.

items.title: eBPF Networking
items.why: Hook points for packet processing and load balancing — the side of eBPF the versus-iptables questions are about. Do this before the opensnoop warm-up if time is short.

items.title: eBPF Datapath: Introduction
items.why: XDP, tc and socket hooks, and why this beats iptables at scale.

items.title: Practice: Previously wrong
items.why: Clear the backlog before the simulation, not after.

days.title: Simulate, review, measure
days.summary: No new material today. Sit the paper under time, review every wrong answer against its citation, then retake the blind set.

items.title: Exam simulation
items.meta: In this app · 60 questions, 90 minutes, 75% to pass
items.why: Timing is the thing reading cannot teach you. 90 seconds a question.

items.title: Review every wrong answer and its citation
items.meta: In this app · results screen links to the docs
items.why: Each wrong answer carries the passage that settles it. Read the passage, not just the explanation.

items.title: Blind evaluation: final
items.meta: In this app · same 102 questions as day 2
items.why: The delta between this and your baseline is the only honest measure of the week.
